text:
dmitri: ran nsys capture on a 1k seq run that showed a weird spike in total kernel time, attaching quick dump below. looks like two kernels dominate now, not the attn kernel we expected.

maya: thanks — can you paste the top kernel table? quick skim helps. :eyes:

dmitri: top kernels (nsys summary):
```
Top kernels by inclusive time:
1) compact_kv_lookup      42.1%  (new, didn't exist in jan baseline)
2) softmax_dispatch       23.5%
3) fused_attn_kv_shift    15.2%
4) token_split_copy       6.0%
5) cudaLaunchKernel       4.0% (kernel launch overheads aggregated)
```
note: compact_kv_lookup has very low occupancy (~12%) but extremely long wall time per call.

kevin: compact_kv_lookup = the new probing path from kv cache prefetching? we added a dense->sparse fallback last month.

dmitri: yes, it's the sparse-path probe. seems we fall into it a lot for certain shard sizes. trace shows repeated small launches (~200us each).

anna: can you share the nsys timeline snippet of one of those sequences? curious if it's warp-serialize or mem-bound.

infra-bot: uploaded /artifacts/nsys/1755554321/compact_probe_timeline.pbz (8.2MB)

maya: quick notes from the timeline:
- compact_kv_lookup has very high L2 cache miss ratio (samples show >40% L2 miss)
- SM util for that kernel is low (<15%) while memory pipe is saturated (lots of DRAM stall samples)
- we see many tiny cudaLaunchKernel entries chained, which suggests our batching granularity is fragmenting work

kevin: that matches hypothesis: batching heuristics currently split batches by token group leading to many small sparse probes. maybe change heuristics to coalesce probes per shard until X bytes or Y tokens.

dmitri: quick repro command I used: `nsys profile -o compact_run --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=cpu --force-overwrite --range=auto -- python perf_runner.py --seq 1024 --batch 8 --model redwood-lite`

anna: can you also run `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` on a few cases so we can get per-kernel memory ops? nsys sampling is great but nvprof gives more counters for misses.

dmitri: queued nvprof run, will push results to the same artifact dir.

sre-elena: from an SLO perspective, this regression bumped p99 gen latency 18% vs baseline for dedicated. tracking as PERF-261. please link traces to the ticket.

maya: action items: 1) dmitri run nvprof counters and attach 2) kevin prototype coalescing probe heuristic (heuristic: merge probes for same shard until total kv-keys >= 512 or time >= 1ms) 3) anna and I will model L2 prefetch hints to reduce DRAM stalls 4) infra will add a microbench that isolates compact_kv_lookup to run in a tight loop for better signal.

kevin: ok on prototype, I'll send a short branch and perf numbers by EOD. if coalescing reduces launch count, should drop launch overhead and improve occupancy.

dmitri: one more oddity — the softmax_dispatch is also heavier than baseline by ~10%, maybe due to different tensor shapes caused by batching change. looking into whether compact path affects downstream shapes.

maya: good call. let's keep an eye on shape skewing. could be we increased padding or fragmentation.

sre-elena: tagging this thread on the ticket. :white_check_mark: small wins here will help p99 quickly.

kevin: FYI I found a micro-optimization: doing keys-first aggregation reduces duplicated probe reads. prototype yields -28% time on compact_kv_lookup in local microbench. pushing patch for review.

dmitri: awesome, thanks. I'll re-run full trace once the branch lands.

maya: thanks all — please drop final artifacts in PERF-261 and ping here when nvprof is uploaded. :rocket:
